absent: Event allocation, permission evaluation, context lookup and pinning, clock setup, output linkage, size validation, auxiliary lookup and exclusivity predicate internals are not shown.
Installation, removal, descheduling, scheduling, overflow handling and file operation table behavior beyond type checks are not shown.
Struct definitions, field offsets, counter layouts, header size computation and sample data formats are not shown.
Hotplug interaction, RCU lifetime rules for units, security hook policy and capability model details are not shown.
Error priority among concurrent validation failures and user visible attribute flag encodings beyond the cgroup selector are not shown.

findings.text: User request to create a counting or sampling event yields a descriptor on success and a negative failure indication otherwise, with target selection distinguishing task versus cpu versus cgroup scope and with optional grouping, output linkage and clock choice.
Sampling use is refused when the underlying measurement unit advertises inability to interrupt, and software marking is applied when the unit belongs to the software context.

Group formation requires the proposed leader to be self led, to share clock and cpu assignment and surrounding context with the newcomer, to remain above exit state, and to carry no exclusive or pinned request on the newcomer itself.

Software members may join a hardware group, while adding hardware to a pure software collection triggers relocation of the whole collection toward hardware handling, and mixing hardware from distinct units outside software is refused.

Per task creation holds the execution update guard for reading across permission validation and later installation, serializing against concurrent image change and credential alteration, with release on every failure path.

Context mutation is serialized by the context mutex, guarding tombstone checks, cpu online checks, group validation, exclusivity checks, header size precalculation and installation, with ordered release and reference drops on failure.

Validation ordering places output linkage, size, auxiliary dependency and exclusivity checks under the same context guard before anonymous file creation, after which failure is no longer permitted and later steps mutate live state.

Group relocation removes leader and siblings and releases old unit references, then reinstalls siblings before leader with fresh state so that leader driven enabling cannot observe siblings in the prior context.

Kernel internal creation provides a direct event handle without descriptor or grouping, enforcing unit lifetime guarding and performing context lookup, tombstone and online validation, exclusivity check and immediate installation.
Kernel creation refuses auxiliary output or action requests and marks ownership with a tombstone value to distinguish internal handles from user owned handles.

Migration of all events of one measurement unit between cpus detaches pinned then flexible members from the source, waits for read side quiescence when anything moved, and reinstalls siblings before leaders at the destination with updated assignment.

Migration holds both source and destination context mutexes together while detaching and reinstalling, and acquires an extra reference on the destination before updating membership so the prior context is released only after the new linkage is visible.

Migrated members that were at least in the off condition are normalized to inactive before installation, ensuring they reenter scheduling quiescent but ready rather than preserving prior active placement.

Task context teardown deschedules when exiting, clears the task linkage, marks the context with a tombstone under lock, optionally emits exit records, then walks remaining members for individual exit handling before releasing the guard.

Teardown holds the context mutex across descheduling and member exit to serialize against most accessors, while creation paths perform lookup without that guard and rely on installation time checks instead.
Non exit teardown for a task awaiting reuse waits until the context reference count returns to a single holder, ensuring prior kernel references and their task pointers have been dropped.

Task exit clears ownership linkage under the owner guard with release ordering, tears down the task context with exit reporting, forwards exit records to cpu wide contexts, and detaches system wide data.

File based lookup helpers validate use of the perf operations table before returning the file or its private event, and attribute access returns the embedded configuration or failure for a null handle.
Delayed task release asserts absence of any remaining task context pointer, and task structure release delegates to context teardown in non exit mode without emitting exit records.
Tracepoint permission combines a paranoid level check with a privilege test and delegates to the security hook, denying when the level is restrictive and privilege is absent.

Inheritance links new members to the original ancestor rather than intermediate parents, skips revoked or exited ancestry, clones configuration for the child task, and mirrors enabled versus disabled condition from the observed parent state.

Inherited frequency mode copies sampling period values into period and budget state, duplicates overflow callback and context pointer, precomputes header sizes, and joins the child context with a child attachment mark under lock.

Inheritance serializes orphan checks and reference acquisition against concurrent release by holding the parent child guard while linking the newcomer into the parent child collection, abandoning creation when orphaned or unreferenced.

Group inheritance creates a leader first then one member per sibling, tolerates a missing leader due to orphaning by producing standalone members, and validates auxiliary linkage between siblings and the new leader.

Per task inheritance during cloning respects flags for general inheritance, thread only inheritance versus clone mode, and signal trap versus cleared handlers, allocating a child context on demand and recording whether all members transferred.
Reuse across differing measurement units or cpus, recursive nesting, clock mismatch, or installation into a tombstoned or offline target aborts creation without mutating live state.

Creation reports conventional failures including permission, invalid argument, missing device or search target, busy exclusive conflict, unsupported sampling, oversize payload and bad descriptor, with success indicated by a fresh descriptor or valid handle.
A dedicated flag selects interpretation of the identifier argument as a cgroup descriptor during target resolution, distinguishing cgroup scoped creation from task or cpu scoped creation.
